title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a combinatorial-homotopical model of the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}. D_d is the closed boundary locus of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification where the curve has at least d nodes, handled via its normalisation and as a stack. D*_d is the open stratum with exactly d nodes. Over D_d sits a G_d-torsor P_d, with G_d an 'extended' analytic torus group, roughly (C*)^d twisted by permutations of the nodes. P*_d is essentially the punctured normal bundle, i.e. a deleted tubular neighbourhood of the stratum.

The index set (d_0 ≥ d_1 ≥ … ≥ d_r) labels chains of strata, i.e. r-simplices of the nerve of the stratification. D_{d_0,…,d_r} maps to D_{d_0} by the 'first component' map, and all the data are pulled back along it: P_{d_0..d_r} on the previous page (207), G_{d_0..d_r} (208). On the previous page (209), the fundamental groupoid Π̃ = Π_1 P*_{d_0..d_r} maps to Π = Π_1 D*_{d_0..d_r}, and that square is 2-cartesian over the d_0 level.

On this page Grothendieck observes the following. The vertical maps of (209) are morphisms of groupoid extensions. Their kernels are twisted Z^{d_0}, namely the local system T_{d_0} of π_1 (equivalently H_1) of the torus fibres. Topologically, T_{d_0} is the lattice spanned by the Dehn twists around the d_0 vanishing cycles, twisted by the monodromy that permutes the nodes.

(210) defines T_{d_0..d_r} as the pullback of T_{d_0}, and T* as its restriction to D*. Hence Π̃_{d_0..d_r} is an extension of Π_{d_0..d_r} by T*. The marginal note 'π_2(D_{d_0..d_r}) = 0' records the hypothesis needed for injectivity of the kernel in the homotopy exact sequence π_2(B) → π_1(F) → π_1(E) → π_1(B). That hypothesis holds because the strata are, up to finite covers, products of moduli spaces M_{g',n'}, which are aspherical orbifolds (Teichmüller spaces are contractible).

(211) packages everything over the simplicial level Δ_r as disjoint unions: the group G_{Δ_r} over D_{Δ_r}, the torsor P_{Δ_r} under it, the local system T_{Δ_r}, and their restrictions to D*_{Δ_r}.

The purpose, continued on the next page, is to get a simplicial system of groupoid extensions Π̃_{Δ_r} → Π_{Δ_r} with kernel T_{Δ_r}. This is a combinatorial model of the homotopy type of the 'boundary at infinity' (a deleted neighbourhood of the boundary) of M_{g,ν}, presumably as a homotopy colimit over the nerve of the stratification. It belongs to the programme of the Esquisse (Teichmüller tower, fundamental groupoids at infinity, Dehn-twist inertia).
errors: Indexing inconsistency: (211) uses d_0 ≥ d_1 ≥ … ≥ d_r, while the next page's (214) uses strict inequalities d_0 > … > d_r. Either degenerate simplices are being dropped or one of the two is a slip.
In (211), 'torseur sur G_{Δr}' should read torsor *under* G_{Δr}, over D_{Δr}; the image appears to say 'torseurs sous G_{Δr}'.
Injectivity of T* into Π̃ needs π_2 of the base to vanish (in the orbifold/stack sense). Grothendieck only flags this in the margin; it is true for the strata of M̄_{g,ν}, but it is not proved here.

Mild ambiguity: T_{d_0..d_r} is defined on the closed D_{d_0..d_r}, while the extension statement uses T* on D*. This is consistent only if the torsor P (and the 'extended' group G) are defined on all of D, with the torus part used on D*.

ideas.what: The fundamental groupoid of the deleted tubular neighbourhood (punctured normal torus bundle) of a boundary stratum is an extension of the stratum's fundamental groupoid by the twisted lattice Z^d generated by the vanishing cycles / Dehn twists.
ideas.modern_name: Local fundamental group at the boundary of M̄_{g,n}; Dehn-twist (inertia) subgroups; stabilisers of simplices of the curve complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Harvey (curve complex, 1970s), Ivanov, Boggi, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps and others for the profinite versions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and the 'structure at infinity' only qualitatively

ideas.what: Pulling torsors, groups and local systems back along the 'first component' maps D_{d_0..d_r} → D_{d_0}, and assembling them over chains of strata into simplicial objects D_{Δ_r}, G_{Δ_r}, P_{Δ_r}, T_{Δ_r}.
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of the stratification poset; homotopy-colimit (Deligne / Clemens-complex style) model of the neighbourhood at infinity of a normal-crossings boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (simplicial resolutions in Hodge II/III), later the exit-path / stratified-homotopy literature

ideas.what: Marginal check that π_2 of the strata vanishes, ensuring the torus-fibre π_1 injects.
ideas.modern_name: Asphericity of moduli stacks M_{g,n} (K(π,1) property)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Teichmüller theory (contractibility of Teichmüller space), standard

missed.claim: The page sets up an explicit simplicial (indexed by chains of boundary strata) system of groupoid extensions Π̃_{Δ_r} → Π_{Δ_r} with Dehn-twist kernels T_{Δ_r}, as a discrete model of the homotopy type at infinity of M_{g,ν}. This is close to later profinite-Teichmüller and curve-complex descriptions (Boggi) and to stratified homotopy / exit-path models, but organised as Deligne-style simplicial descent of torsors.
missed.quote: disant que Π̃_{d0,…,dr} est une ext. de Π_{d0,…,dr} par T*_{d0…dr}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck had a concrete simplicial/descent formalism for the boundary homotopy type. That is of historical interest for the Esquisse programme, but the mathematical content is by now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful bookkeeping definitions (pullbacks, restrictions, disjoint unions) of a standard picture: the Dehn-twist lattice as kernel of the boundary fundamental group. The only mildly notable feature is the simplicial packaging over chains of strata, an early instance of a now-standard approach.

(210): the struck-out left-hand side reads roughly 'T̃*_{d_0,Z,d_r}' (crossed out), and the line continues '≃ syst. local des π_1 (ou des H_1) des fibres de P_{d_0…d_r} sur D_{d_0…d_r}'; the final '[?]' looks like a subscript on D.
(211): 'torseur sur G_{Δr}' should read 'torseurs sous G_{Δr}'.
(211): an extra struck-out subscript line 'd_?…≥d_0' appears under the coproduct, above '(d_0,…,d_r) ∈ N^{r+1}'.
Bottom of (211): 'système local des π_1, ou H_1, de G_{Δr} ou P_{Δr}, au choix'; then 'G*_{Δr}, P*_{Δr}, T*_{Δr} les restrictions à D*_{Δr}'.

Top margin: approximately 'π_1 de D_{d_0} & de D*_{d_0} … dans variation …'. The second margin note, around 'π_2(D_{d_0..d_r}) = 0', is likewise prefixed 'dans variation …'; both are partly illegible.
